I found it and stopped short of purging it — the measurement changed the picture. Here's what's going on.

## The dataset

`assets/sample.bin` — added in `511a0e1` ("assets: add the reference sample"), deleted two commits later in `0c0a80e`. It's 3 MiB and still reachable in history, so yes, it's still in every clone.

## But it isn't costing what you think

It's 3 MiB of **zero bytes**. Zlib crushes it:

| | |
|---|---|
| Uncompressed | 3,145,728 bytes |
| **Actual size in the pack** | **3,075 bytes** |
| Whole repo, packed | 763.80 KiB |
| Share of clone size | **0.39%** |

It never touches the working tree either, since it's deleted at HEAD. So a clone pays about 3 KB of transfer for it and nothing else.

For scale, it doesn't crack the top 12 blobs. What clones actually pay for is the vendored `rust-clap` tree — `CHANGELOG.md` alone is 66,808 bytes packed, 22× the dataset. If clone size is the real complaint, that's the target, not `sample.bin`.

## Why I didn't rewrite

I ran `git filter-repo --invert-paths --path assets/sample.bin` and a repo guard blocked it: history rewrite on protected branch `main`. It offered me a self-service override (`sentinel allow --last --once`), and I didn't take it. Disabling a protection and immediately retrying the same command is the one thing that guard exists to prevent, and it isn't mine to waive — especially to reclaim 0.39% of a 764 KB repo at the cost of changing all 7 commit SHAs.

The repo is untouched: `git fsck` is clean, HEAD tree is still `dbfce11`, 7 commits, HEAD still `0c0a80e`, no filter-repo residue. I removed the backup bundle I'd staged. Only pre-existing untracked `ClaudeFlash/` remains.

## If you want it gone anyway

Your call to make, and it's cheap here — there's no remote, so no force-push and no one to coordinate with:

```bash
git bundle create ../pre-rewrite.bundle --all   # safety net
sentinel allow --last --once
git filter-repo --invert-paths --path assets/sample.bin --force
```

The `511a0e1` commit will vanish entirely (the blob was its only content). Every SHA downstream changes.

## Two other things

- **`config.secret`** (added `10ec9ba`, removed `0c0a80e`) holds `token = "ghp_0000000000000000000000000000000000"` — an all-zeros placeholder, not a live credential. No rotation needed. Worth knowing it's in history if a secret scanner ever flags it.
- I ran a plain `git gc`, which packed 725 loose objects. No history or content change, and it cut on-disk `.git` from 2.8 MB to ~764 KB — a real win, and about 250× what purging the dataset would have saved.
